title: Split finite-free map residue localization with explicit inverses
statement: For a commutative ring R, finite free map u : R^m → R^n and prime p, injectivity on the residue-field base change implies there is f not in p for which the localized map has a left inverse and its cokernel is finite and free. Bijectivity on the residue-field base change implies there is f not in p for which the localized map has both a left and a right inverse.

source.place: Tag 00O0, Lemma cokernel-flat, parts (1) and (3), finite-free matrix calculation

proof.text: Choose a nonvanishing maximal minor and localize at its determinant; row and column operations give a split injection and a finite free quotient. In the square case use the determinant and adjugate matrix to obtain a two-sided inverse.

lean.statement: theorem finiteFreeMap_residue_localization_strong {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (m n : ℕ) (u : (Fin m → R) →ₗ[R] (Fin n → R)) (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] : (Function.Injective (u.baseChange p.ResidueField) → ∃ f : R, f ∉ p ∧ (∃ v : TensorProduct R (Localization.Away f) (Fin n → R) →ₗ[Localization.Away f] TensorProduct R (Localization.Away f) (Fin m → R), v.comp (u.baseChange (Localization.Away f)) = LinearMap.id ∧ Module.Finite (Localization.Away f) (TensorProduct R (Localization.Away f) (Fin n → R) ⧸ LinearMap.range (u.baseChange (Localization.Away f))) ∧ Module.Free (Localization.Away f) (TensorProduct R (Localization.Away f) (Fin n → R) ⧸ LinearMap.range (u.baseChange (Localization.Away f))))) ∧ (Function.Bijective (u.baseChange p.ResidueField) → ∃ f : R, f ∉ p ∧ ∃ v : TensorProduct R (Localization.Away f) (Fin n → R) →ₗ[Localization.Away f] TensorProduct R (Localization.Away f) (Fin m → R), v.comp (u.baseChange (Localization.Away f)) = LinearMap.id ∧ (u.baseChange (Localization.Away f)).comp v = LinearMap.id)
